title: Coupled resonators: loading, voltage gain and the complete source budget
question: Can passive magnetically coupled resonators produce receiver voltage above source voltage while all receiver power remains accounted for by the source and losses?
incoming_evidence: Atlas V4 checked a single RLC circuit but not a coupled receiver or reflected source impedance. Tesla's coupled tuning is a source-grounded mechanism; it does not imply source-free energy.

historical_lenses.Tesla: Specify coupled coils, phase, receiver loading and return paths.
historical_lenses.Newton: Reconstruct a cause from observed receiver voltage only after testing alternative source/loading explanations.

source_records.reading_status_at_freeze: Skill reference selected passages; source agent will separately document direct project reading
Recovered prior project result in session; no physical data

classification: Modern reconstruction and synthetic circuit fixture, not Tesla's numerical apparatus, new law, measured efficiency or proof of energy extraction from vacuum.

state_and_units.R: series resistances including receiver load, ohm

model.phasor: Z(omega) I = (V,0); Z11=R1+i(omega L1-1/(omega C1)); Z22=R2+RL+i(omega L2-1/(omega C2)); Z12=Z21=i omega M. Phasors are peak amplitudes; average power uses 1/2.
model.transient: qdot=i; L idot=(Vpeak sin(omega0 t),0)-diag(R1,R2+RL)i-diag(1/C1,1/C2)q; q(0)=i(0)=0.
model.storage: E=(i^T L i + q^T diag(1/C)q)/2, with |k|<1 ensuring positive definite L.
model.budget: Psource=Re(V conjugate(I1))/2; Pload=RL |I2|^2/2; Ploss=(R1|I1|^2+R2|I2|^2)/2. Finite-time source work = load heat + winding heat + stored-energy change.
model.boundary: Ideal sinusoidal source, lumped linear elements, no core hysteresis, stray capacitance, radiation, temperature dependence, source impedance beyond R1, sensor loading or environmental drive.

observables: Receiver power/source real power for nonzero source power
Reflected impedance and complete transient work balance
rival_explanations: Voltage gain is an impedance/phase effect supplied by source power
Apparent excess could arise by comparing peak voltage to real power or omitting source backaction
controls: Zero coupling gives zero receiver response
Zero source gives zero phasor response
Reverse M: receiver phase flips by pi; powers unchanged
At common uncoupled resonance, compare complex currents against closed-form reflected-resistance expression
Double both winding resistances and inspect efficiency reduction at fixed omega0 and nominal RL
Two transient sample spacings and tighter solver tolerance; perform external Simpson work quadrature, not only integrated work states

acceptance.gain_witness: Report at least one fixed parameter row with voltage gain >1 AND efficiency <=1; if absent report failure rather than tune beyond frozen domain.

falsifier: Any reproducible passive-model budget violation beyond declared tolerance rejects this implementation; voltage gain alone cannot support a free-energy claim.
limits: Finite fixture and frequency/load grid are not a global optimization theorem
No apparatus has been built or measured
The lumped circuit has no gravity or cosmological degree of freedom
next_round_rule: Independent review selects the next question. Candidate only: whether phase-resolved two-channel readout can localize a drive once this forward model is checked. Do not execute before the R1B review.
